card: This PR replaces dedicated out-of-band interrupt methods on the mining IPC interface with cancellation arguments on blocking calls (waitTipChanged, createNewBlock, and waitNext). It allows IPC clients such as Stratum v2 services to cancel in-flight blocking requests natively by dropping Cap'n Proto promises. The change implements the design agreed upon in RFC #33575. It depends on upstream libmultiprocess#342, included here as a temporary subtree commit.
changed_since_previous: Rebased and updated against newer libmultiprocess subtree commits.
evidence: PR description: 'The blocking methods (waitTipChanged, createNewBlock, and BlockTemplate::waitNext) currently rely on interrupt()/interruptWait() to cancel them when they are in progress (#33676, #34184). With request cancellation support in libmultiprocess (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#342), this is no longer needed.'
PR description: 'Additional note: this is the Bitcoin Core side of approach 4 in #33575.'
problem: Canceling in-flight blocking mining interface calls over IPC requires separate, out-of-band interrupt calls that add API complexity and extra round-trips, making targeted cancellation of individual requests cumbersome.

risk.why: Mistakes in IPC request cancellation or callback lifecycle management could trigger use-after-free conditions or leave mining calls permanently blocked.

scope_notes: Contains a temporary commit updating the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree to include unmerged changes from libmultiprocess PR #342.
summary: Add cancellation arguments (`CancelArg`) to blocking mining interface methods (`waitTipChanged`, `createNewBlock`, and `BlockTemplate::waitNext`), deprecating `interrupt()` and `interruptWait()`. Using Cap'n Proto request cancellation via annotations in `mining.capnp`, in-flight IPC calls can be canceled directly by dropping the request promise rather than issuing separate interrupt calls.
